title: The Injection Point
summary: A little web tool runs a command for you, and it doesn't check what you type. That is your way in; a password it lets you read is your account; a careless sudo rule is root.
story: Juniper Health (made up) runs an internal tools site, app01, on 10.10.5.0/24. You start on scout. The site has a ping page that staff use to check if a host is reachable.
goal: Capture the user flag in the appsvc home folder and the root flag in /root.
skills: web recon, command injection, reading a config as the web account, ssh, sudo -l

hints.text: Scan app01 and open its web page. The ping tool takes a host in the URL: /tools/ping?host=127.0.0.1. It tells you it runs ping -c1 with whatever you give it.
The tool doesn't check its input, so extra shell characters run extra commands as the web account: try host=127.0.0.1;id . Use ; ls and ; cat to look around for a config file.
The web account can read /var/www/conf/app.ini, which holds the appsvc password. ssh appsvc@10.10.5.30 with it, then sudo -l: sed can read any file as root.
